CSS requires the x coordinates of a cubic-bezier to stay within 0 and 1 because time cannot go backward. The y values may overshoot, which is how ease-out-back effects work. This tool clamps x1 and x2 to the valid range.

faq.q: What is the difference between ease-in and ease-out?
faq.a: Ease-in starts slow and accelerates, which feels like something powering up. Ease-out starts fast and decelerates, which feels responsive and is the better default for UI feedback like buttons and menus.

faq.q: How do I get a bouncy spring effect?
faq.a: Push y1 above 1 or y2 below 0 so the curve overshoots. Try cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1), the classic ease-out-back: it sails slightly past the target then settles.

faq.q: Can I use cubic-bezier for animations too?
faq.a: Yes, animation-timing-function accepts the same values as transition-timing-function. The copied CSS shows both forms so you can paste whichever your project uses.

faq.q: Why does my animation look robotic with linear?
faq.a: Linear moves at constant speed, which real objects never do. Physical motion always accelerates and decelerates. Even a subtle ease-out makes interface motion feel dramatically more natural.

faq.q: How long should a UI transition be?
faq.a: 150 to 300ms for hover feedback and small UI changes, 400 to 600ms for panels and page transitions. Longer than a second feels sluggish unless it is a deliberate showcase animation.

faq.a: Shake, played once over 0.4 to 0.5 seconds. The quick lateral motion reads as no without needing any text, and stopping after one play keeps it from feeling aggressive.

faq.q: How do I chain two animations on one element?

faq.q: Can I pause the animation on hover?

faq.q: What does ease-in-out do in the shorthand?
faq.a: It smooths both ends of each iteration so the motion accelerates out of each keyframe and decelerates into the next. For spins and pulses it removes the visible snap when the loop restarts.

Vintage: sepia 40 percent plus contrast 90 percent. Noir: grayscale 100 percent plus contrast 130 percent. Dreamy: brightness 110 percent plus saturate 130 percent plus a touch of blur. Start from these recipes, then tune by eye.

faq.q: Do CSS filters work on background images?
faq.a: Yes, but filter applies to the whole element including its children. To filter only a background, put the image on a pseudo-element or a dedicated layer and filter that layer alone.

faq.q: Are CSS filters GPU accelerated?
faq.a: Mostly yes in modern browsers, which is why hover filter transitions stay smooth. Very large blurred areas can still cost performance on low-end phones, so test on real devices.

faq.q: Can I animate between two filters?
faq.a: Yes, filter is animatable: transition: filter 0.4s gives smooth cross-fades between states, which is how image galleries do elegant hover colorizations.

faq.q: Why does hue-rotate change all my colors?
faq.a: Hue-rotate spins every hue in the image around the color wheel by the given degrees. 180deg turns blues orange and reds cyan. It is the fastest way to recolor an entire illustration.

faq.q: What is the difference between opacity filter and opacity property?
faq.a: Visually almost none for a single element. The filter version participates in the filter pipeline and can be combined with other effects in one animatable property, which is convenient for hover states.

Directional resize cursors like nwse-resize and ew-resize tell users exactly which way a handle drags. Use them on splitters, resizable panels and crop handles. The bidirectional pairs cover diagonals, the single-axis ones cover straight edges.

faq.q: When should I use cursor: pointer?
faq.a: On anything clickable that is not a native link or button: cards, table rows, custom dropdowns. Native buttons and links already show pointer by default, so you rarely need to set it on those.

faq.q: What is the difference between grab and move?
faq.a: Grab signals something draggable but not yet dragged, like a map or kanban card; grabbing shows while dragging. Move is the older generic dragging cursor. Prefer the grab pair for modern draggable UIs.

faq.q: Can I use a custom image as a cursor?
faq.a: Yes: cursor: url(pointer.png) 8 8, pointer. The numbers set the hotspot. Keep a keyword fallback after the URL for browsers that reject the image, and keep the file under 128px.

faq.q: Why does cursor: none exist?
faq.a: It hides the cursor, useful for drawing apps, games and fullscreen video where the system arrow would distract. Always provide an obvious way to get it back, like pressing Escape.

faq.q: Do cursors matter on touch devices?
faq.a: No, touch screens have no hover cursor, so never rely on cursor changes alone to communicate meaning. Pair every cursor cue with a visible affordance like an underline or icon.

Modern responsive design also adapts to user preferences: prefers-color-scheme for dark mode, prefers-reduced-motion to disable animation for sensitive users, and print to restyle pages for paper. These ship alongside breakpoint queries in a mature stylesheet.

faq.q: Which breakpoints should I actually use?
faq.a: Use content-based breakpoints: resize your browser until the layout breaks, then set a query there. The presets here (640, 768, 1024, 1280, 1536) match Tailwind defaults and are a fine starting point for most sites.

faq.q: Why is my max-width query not applying?
faq.a: Check the order: later rules win at equal specificity, so max-width queries should come after your base styles. Also verify the viewport meta tag is present, without it phones report a fake 980px width.

faq.q: Should I still support print styles?
faq.a: If users print invoices, tickets, articles or resumes from your site, yes. A minimal print query hides navigation and ads, sets black-on-white text, and avoids background colors that waste ink.

faq.q: What does the retina query do?
faq.a: It targets screens with 2x pixel density and up, where you can serve sharper background images or thinner borders. Use min-resolution: 192dpi as the standard syntax with the webkit prefix for older Safari.

faq.q: How do I test dark mode queries?
faq.a: In Chrome DevTools open the rendering panel and emulate prefers-color-scheme: dark. On macOS you can also toggle the system appearance; the query follows the OS setting live.

explainer.body: The score blends seven checks email marketers actually use: character length, word count, spam-trigger words, all-caps shouting, exclamation mark abuse, personalization signals and scannability. Each failed check costs 12 points, so a subject failing three checks lands around 64, which matches how picky inbox filters are.

explainer.h: Why 50 characters is the magic number
explainer.body: Most mobile email apps cut subject lines around 40 to 50 characters. Desktop Gmail shows about 70. Writing under 50 guarantees your full message and your call to action survive on the smallest screen, which is where most opens happen.

faq.q: What words trigger spam filters?
faq.a: Classic triggers include free, guaranteed, winner, cash prize, act now, risk-free and no cost, plus ALL CAPS and multiple exclamation marks. Filters score combinations, so one mild word is fine but three together is risky.

faq.q: Does personalization really lift open rates?
faq.a: Yes. Subject lines with the recipient's name or a relevant you-phrase consistently outperform generic ones by 20 to 30 percent in most industry studies. Relevance beats cleverness in the inbox.

faq.q: How long should a subject line be?
faq.a: 20 to 50 characters, or 3 to 10 words. Shorter than 20 often lacks a clear promise; longer than 50 gets truncated on phones and dilutes the message.

faq.q: Should I use emojis in subject lines?
faq.a: One relevant emoji can lift opens in B2C, but they render inconsistently across email clients and can trip strict corporate filters. Test with your audience before making them a habit.

faq.q: How many exclamation marks are too many?
faq.a: More than one. A single exclamation mark is acceptable for genuine excitement; two or more reads as spam to both filters and humans. When in doubt, use a period or nothing.

faq.a: Full international format with country code, digits only: 6281234567890 for Indonesia, 14155552671 for the US. Drop the leading plus, spaces, dashes and any leading zero after the country code.

faq.q: Does the person need to save my number first?

faq.q: Can I use this for a business WhatsApp number?

faq.q: Why is my prefilled message showing weird characters?

faq.q: Can I track clicks on my WhatsApp link?
faq.a: wa.me links have no built-in analytics. Route the link through a shortener like bit.ly or your own redirect with UTM parameters if you need click counts.

faq.q: Does the recipient need my contact?

faq.q: Can I prefill a link to a Telegram channel?
faq.a: Yes, put the channel invite link or public t.me link in the URL field. Recipients tap it inside Telegram and land straight on the channel.

faq.q: Why is my text showing encoded characters?

faq.q: Can I add hashtags to the shared text?

faq.q: Do share links work on desktop Telegram?

faq.q: Why does the link open the wrong email app?
faq.a: mailto links open the system's default email client, which the user controls. On phones it is usually Gmail or Apple Mail; on desktops it may be Outlook or Thunderbird.

faq.q: Is there a length limit for mailto links?
faq.a: Practically yes: keep the whole link under about 2000 characters. Very long prefilled bodies can get truncated by some browsers, so keep bodies concise.

faq.q: Can mailto include HTML formatting?
faq.a: No. The body parameter is plain text only; HTML tags will show as literal text. For rich formatted emails you need a backend mail service, not a mailto link.

faq.q: Do mailto links expose my email to spammers?
faq.a: Yes, any email address in page HTML can be harvested by bots. For public pages consider a contact form instead, or obfuscate the address with JavaScript.

faq.q: Does the visitor need a Google account?
faq.a: Yes, to save the event they need to be signed into Google. The link still shows the event details to signed-out users and prompts them to sign in, so it degrades gracefully.

faq.q: Can I make an all-day event?
faq.a: Yes: use the date-only format YYYYMMDD/YYYYMMDD in the dates parameter instead of the datetime form. This tool focuses on timed events, which cover webinars and meetings.

faq.q: How do I add the event to Outlook instead?
faq.a: Outlook on the web accepts a similar deep link, and Apple Calendar users can subscribe via .ics files. Google template links cover the largest audience; offer an .ics download alongside for the rest.

faq.q: Why is my event an hour off?
faq.a: The link has no timezone data, so daylight saving transitions or a mis-set device clock shift it. Double-check the start and end times in the generated link before publishing.

faq.q: Can I prefill guests on the event?
faq.a: Google's template endpoint supports an add parameter with comma-separated emails. It is undocumented and occasionally ignored, so mention key guests in the description as a backup.

faq.q: Where do I find my PayPal.me username?
faq.a: In PayPal go to Settings, then PayPal.me, or visit paypal.me and create your link. It is usually your name or business name; you cannot change it later, so pick carefully.

faq.q: Do I pay fees on PayPal.me payments?
faq.a: Payments marked as goods and services carry PayPal's standard receiving fee, which varies by country. Friends and family payments are usually free domestically. Check PayPal's fee page for your region.

faq.q: Can buyers pay without a PayPal account?

faq.q: What currencies can I request?
faq.a: PayPal supports 25 plus currencies on PayPal.me links. The payer is charged in the link currency and PayPal converts if their balance differs, showing the conversion before they confirm.

faq.q: Is it safe to post my PayPal.me link publicly?
faq.a: Reasonably. It reveals only your chosen username, not your email or balance. Still, watch for fake payment confirmation emails, the classic scam against public payment links.

explainer.body: Drive share URLs point at a preview page with a download button. The uc?export=download&id= endpoint serves the file bytes directly, so browsers start downloading immediately instead of rendering the preview UI. The file ID is the long token in the middle of the share URL.

Very large files trigger a virus-scan warning page that breaks the direct flow, and files shared only with specific people require sign-in. For public assets under a few hundred MB shared as anyone with the link, the direct URL works reliably.

faq.q: Which Drive link formats are supported?
faq.a: Both common formats: drive.google.com/file/d/FILE_ID/view and drive.google.com/open?id=FILE_ID. You can also paste just the bare file ID itself and the tool will build the link.

faq.q: Why does the download show a virus scan warning?
faq.a: Google scans files it cannot verify and shows an interstitial for executables and archives over 100 MB. Users click through once; the file itself is unaffected.

faq.q: Can I use the direct link as an image embed?
faq.a: For small public images, yes: the direct URL works in img tags. For reliable hotlinking at scale use proper hosting instead, since Drive throttles heavy traffic with 403 errors.

faq.q: Does the direct link work for folders?
faq.a: No, only single files. Folders have no direct download endpoint; share the folder link normally or zip the folder first, then share the zip file.

faq.q: Will the link break if I move the file?
faq.a: No. The file ID stays constant when you move or rename a file within Drive. The link only breaks if you delete the file or change its sharing to private.

explainer.body: YouTube reads a t parameter in seconds: watch?v=ID&t=90s starts 90 seconds in. The player seeks after load, so the link works in browsers, the mobile app and embeds alike. Hours work too: 1:02:30 becomes 3750 seconds.

YouTube URLs come in many forms: watch pages, youtu.be shorts, /shorts/ paths and /embed/ paths. This tool extracts the 11-character video ID from all of them and rebuilds a clean canonical watch URL with the timestamp attached.

faq.q: What timestamp formats are accepted?
faq.a: Plain seconds (90), minutes and seconds (1:30), or hours, minutes and seconds (1:02:30). Anything the tool cannot parse gets a clear error instead of a broken link.

faq.q: Do timestamp links work for Shorts?
faq.a: Yes, the generated link uses the standard watch URL which plays the video at your timestamp. Shorts themselves are under 60 seconds, so timestamps matter less there but still work.

faq.q: Can I link to the end of a video instead?
faq.a: There is no end parameter, but you can link near the end with a large timestamp. For looping a segment, use the embed generator with start and end parameters instead.

faq.q: Why does the video start a few seconds off?
faq.a: YouTube seeks to the nearest keyframe, which can be 2 to 5 seconds before your timestamp on some videos. For frame-exact sharing you would need to trim and re-upload the clip.

faq.q: Can I add a timestamp to an embedded video?
faq.a: Yes, append ?start=90 to the embed URL. The embed player accepts start in seconds, and optionally end, which the plain watch URL does not support.

Browsers block autoplay with sound, so the autoplay option here also mutes the player, the only combination browsers allow to start automatically. Users unmute with one click. Autoplaying with sound is not possible without a user gesture, by design.

faq.q: What is privacy-enhanced mode?
faq.a: It loads the player from youtube-nocookie.com, which does not set tracking cookies until the visitor plays the video. Use it on EU sites to reduce cookie-consent headaches.

faq.q: Can I hide the YouTube logo and title?
faq.a: YouTube removed most branding controls; the logo and title now always show on hover. rel=0 limits end-screen suggestions to your own channel instead of hiding them entirely.

faq.q: Why is my embed not responsive?
faq.a: You probably pasted a fixed width and height iframe. The wrapper technique in the generated code makes the player fluid. Replace the whole snippet, not just the src.

faq.q: Do embeds count as views?
faq.a: Yes, embedded plays count toward the public view count when the video actually plays. Autoplay-muted embeds count too, subject to YouTube's normal view validation.

faq.q: Can I start the video at a specific time?
faq.a: Yes, set the start field to seconds. The embed URL carries a start parameter, and you can add end the same way by editing the code if you need a clipped segment.

faq.q: Can I use someone else's thumbnail?
faq.a: Thumbnails are copyrighted by the video owner. Grabbing them for reference or commentary thumbnails is common, but reusing them commercially without permission risks a copyright strike.

faq.q: Why is the maxres image gray?

faq.q: What size should I download for my own video?

faq.q: Do thumbnails work for private videos?
faq.a: No. Thumbnail URLs only resolve for public and unlisted videos. Private video thumbnails require the owner's authenticated session.

faq.q: Can I hotlink the thumbnail URL on my site?
faq.a: Technically yes, and YouTube tolerates it for embeds and previews. For high-traffic sites, download and self-host the image so you are not dependent on their CDN.

explainer.h: Why scenarios matter more than a single number
explainer.body: CTR and CPC swing wildly by niche: finance clicks can pay $2 while entertainment pays $0.10. Showing conservative, expected and optimistic scenarios keeps the estimate honest instead of pretending one number fits every site.

faq.q: What is a good AdSense CTR?
faq.a: 1 to 2 percent is typical for content sites. Above 3 percent is excellent and usually means strong ad placement; below 0.5 percent suggests ads are buried or the audience ignores them.

faq.q: What is a good CPC?
faq.a: It depends entirely on niche and country. Finance and insurance clicks can exceed $2, while general entertainment often sits under $0.15. US, UK and Canadian traffic pays 3 to 5 times more than most other regions.

faq.q: How many pageviews do I need to earn $100 a month?
faq.a: At a 1.5 percent CTR and $0.35 CPC, roughly 19,000 pageviews. With a $1 CPC the same $100 needs only about 6,700 pageviews, which is why niche choice matters more than raw traffic.

faq.q: Does ad placement really change earnings?
faq.a: Yes, dramatically. Ads above the fold and inside content typically double or triple the CTR of footer or sidebar-only placements, without needing a single extra visitor.

faq.q: Why do my real earnings differ from the estimate?
faq.a: Seasonality, invalid click filtering, ad blockers and smart pricing all move the real number. Treat the estimate as a planning baseline, then calibrate with 30 days of your own data.

explainer.body: Your public IP is the address the internet sees when your network makes requests. Home routers share one public IP across every device inside via NAT, while your phone gets a different one on mobile data. Sites, games and APIs use it to route responses back to you.

ipify is a free API that returns your IP as JSON with no key, no signup and no rate games for normal use. Because the fetch happens in your browser, the address never passes through this site's servers at all.

faq.q: Why does my IP change sometimes?
faq.a: Most home connections use dynamic IPs that your ISP rotates every few days or on router reboot. Business lines and servers usually pay for static IPs that never change.

faq.q: Is my IP address private information?
faq.a: Treat it as semi-private. It reveals your ISP and rough city to every site you visit, so avoid posting it publicly, but there is no need to panic about normal browsing.

faq.q: What is the difference between IPv4 and IPv6?
faq.a: IPv4 addresses look like 203.0.113.45 with four number groups; IPv6 uses eight hex groups and is far longer. This tool shows IPv4, which most home connections still use for outbound traffic.

faq.q: Can I hide my IP address?
faq.a: Yes, with a VPN or proxy that routes your traffic through its own servers. Websites then see the VPN's IP instead of yours, at the cost of some speed.

faq.q: Why does the tool need my click instead of auto-detecting?
faq.a: Auto-fetching on page load would ping the API for every visitor including bots. A deliberate click keeps usage fair so the free API stays free for everyone.

faq.q: What is the difference between ISP and organization?

faq.q: Can I look up IPv6 addresses?

faq.q: Is looking up someone's IP legal?
faq.a: Looking up publicly routable IP metadata like ASN and rough location is standard network diagnostics, the same data every website logs. It does not reveal a person's name or exact address.

faq.q: Which country has the most timezones?
faq.a: France, with 12, thanks to its overseas territories spanning the globe. Russia has 11 contiguous zones, the most of any single landmass, and the US has 11 counting territories.

faq.q: Why does Indonesia have three timezones?
faq.a: The archipelago stretches over 5,000 km east to west: WIB (UTC+7) in the west, WITA (UTC+8) in the center, and WIT (UTC+9) in the east. One zone would put sunrise at wildly different clock times.

faq.q: Do all countries observe daylight saving?
faq.a: No, and the trend is away from it. The EU debates abolition yearly, while most of Asia, Africa and South America never adopted it. The dataset reflects standard offsets; check locally for DST.

faq.q: What does UTC+05:30 mean?
faq.a: Five and a half hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time. A few zones use 30 or 45 minute offsets, like India at +05:30 and Nepal at +05:45, historical quirks that stuck.

faq.q: How do I schedule across timezones reliably?
faq.a: Agree on one reference, usually UTC, and let each person's calendar convert. Saying 14:00 UTC leaves no ambiguity; saying 2 PM invites exactly the confusion this tool helps you avoid.

toolUI:
DNS query

Enter a domain and pick a record type.

DNS records

Records appear here.

explainer.body: Traditional DNS is plaintext UDP on port 53, visible to your network. DNS over HTTPS wraps the same query in an encrypted HTTPS request to an endpoint like Cloudflare's, returning JSON instead of binary packets. Your browser does the whole exchange, so no server side is needed for this tool.

A records map a domain to IPv4 addresses, AAAA to IPv6. MX records list mail servers with priorities, TXT holds SPF, DKIM and verification tokens as text, CNAME aliases one name to another, and NS shows which name servers are authoritative for the domain.

faq.q: Why does my domain show no MX records?
faq.a: Then it cannot receive email at that domain. MX records are what sending servers look up; without them, mail bounces. Add them at your DNS provider when you set up Google Workspace or similar.

faq.q: What is a TXT record used for?
faq.a: Domain verification and email authentication: Google site verification tokens, SPF policies that list allowed senders, and DKIM public keys all live in TXT records. They are the most-queried type after A.

faq.q: How long does DNS take to update?
faq.a: Changes propagate as old cached entries expire, governed by the TTL value, commonly 5 minutes to 24 hours. If a record looks stale, wait out the TTL rather than re-saving it repeatedly.

faq.q: CNAME versus A record: which should I use?
faq.a: Use A records for root domains pointing at IPs, and CNAMEs for subdomains aliasing to another hostname, like www to your host. Never put a CNAME on the bare root domain; it breaks MX and NS resolution.

faq.q: Is DNS over HTTPS private?
faq.a: It encrypts the query content from your local network and ISP, but the DoH provider still sees which domains you look up. For this tool that tradeoff is fine: Cloudflare handles billions of such queries daily.

explainer.body: ROI compares what you gained against what you spent: subtract the cost from the total return, divide by the cost, and express it as a percentage. A 50% ROI means you earned half your stake on top of getting it back. The calculator also shows the return multiple (1.5x) and, when you enter a holding period, the annualized rate so multi-year investments can be compared fairly.

Positive ROI means profit, negative means loss, and zero means you broke even. Use ROI to compare opportunities of different sizes, but remember it ignores risk and timing: two investments with the same ROI are not equal if one took five times longer.

faq.q: What is the ROI formula?
faq.a: ROI = (total return minus amount invested) divided by amount invested, times 100. For example, investing $1,000 and getting back $1,500 gives a 50% ROI.

faq.q: What is a good ROI?
faq.a: It depends on the asset. Stock markets have averaged roughly 7 to 10 percent per year historically, so beating that after risk is a common benchmark. Higher returns usually mean higher risk.

faq.q: What does the return multiple mean?
faq.a: It shows how many times your money came back. A 2.5x multiple means every $1 invested returned $2.50 in total, which equals a 150% ROI.

faq.q: What is annualized ROI?
faq.a: It spreads the total return evenly across each year of the holding period using compounding, so a 50% gain over 2 years becomes about 22.5% per year.

faq.q: Does ROI include fees and taxes?
faq.a: Only if you include them in your numbers. For an accurate figure, add purchase fees to the cost and subtract selling fees and taxes from the return before calculating.

explainer.h: Why the string looks so messy
explainer.body: Decades of compatibility hacks are baked in. Nearly every browser still starts with Mozilla/5.0 for historical reasons, then piles on tokens for the rendering engine, OS and device. The readable breakdown below decodes the important parts for you.

faq.q: What is my user agent used for?
faq.a: Websites use it to detect your browser and OS, serve mobile or desktop layouts, offer the right app download, and collect analytics about their visitors.

faq.q: Can websites identify me from it?
faq.a: Partly. The string alone rarely identifies you personally, but combined with screen size, fonts and other signals it contributes to browser fingerprinting.

faq.q: Why does my Chrome user agent mention Safari?
faq.a: For compatibility. Chrome's string includes Safari and KHTML tokens because early sites served better pages to Safari-identified browsers, and the convention stuck.

faq.q: Can I change my user agent?
faq.a: Yes. Most browsers let you override it in developer tools, and extensions can spoof it per site, which is useful for testing how pages look on other devices.

faq.q: Is any of this data sent to a server?
faq.a: No. Everything on this page is read from your browser's own JavaScript APIs and displayed locally.

faq.q: What is the difference between HTML encode and URL encode?

faq.q: Why did my JavaScript unescape fail?
faq.a: The input must be a valid escaped sequence, like text copied from inside quotes in source code. A lone backslash at the end or an invalid \u escape will make parsing fail.

faq.q: Does URL encode handle Unicode?
faq.a: Yes. Characters outside ASCII are encoded as UTF-8 byte sequences, so emoji and non-Latin scripts convert correctly.

faq.q: Is HTML encoding enough to prevent XSS?
faq.a: It is the core defense for text inserted into HTML content. For values placed inside attributes, event handlers or JavaScript contexts, additional context-specific encoding is needed.

faq.q: Is hex encoding the same as encryption?
faq.a: No. Hex is just a different way of writing the same data and is trivially reversible. Never treat it as a way to hide secrets.

faq.q: What is hex used for in real life?
faq.a: Displaying cryptographic hashes, color codes like #ff5c8a, binary file dumps, MAC addresses and debugging network data.

explainer.body: Line-height (leading) is the vertical space between lines of text. Too tight and lines collide into an unreadable wall; too loose and the eye loses its place jumping between lines. For body text, ratios between 1.4 and 1.75 hit the comfort zone, with 1.5 the classic default.

CSS best practice is a unitless ratio like line-height: 1.5, which scales with the font size automatically, even for nested elements. Pixel values lock the height and break when text is resized. The table shows both so you can see the math, but copy the unitless version.

faq.a: 1.618 is a classical proportion some designers use for vertical rhythm. It is a fine choice, but comfort testing beats numerology.

faq.q: Why unitless instead of px?
faq.a: A unitless value multiplies whatever font size is in effect, so nested or resized text keeps proportional spacing. Pixel values do not adapt.

faq.q: Does line-height affect accessibility?
faq.a: Yes. WCAG recommends enough spacing that text remains readable, and users who enlarge text depend on proportional line-height to keep it legible.

faq.q: Does resolution affect file size?
faq.a: Only indirectly. Size is set by bitrate and duration. Resolution matters for quality: the same bitrate spread over more pixels (4K) looks worse per pixel than over fewer (1080p).

faq.q: What bitrate should I use for YouTube 1080p?
faq.a: YouTube recommends 8 Mbps for standard 1080p and up to 12 Mbps for high-motion content. The presets include common platform recommendations as starting points.

faq.q: What is the difference between 301 and 302?
faq.a: 301 means the move is permanent: browsers and search engines should remember the new URL. 302 is temporary: keep using the old URL next time. Use 308/307 when the request method must not change.

faq.q: Why do I get 403 instead of 401?
faq.a: 401 means you are not authenticated (log in and retry). 403 means you are authenticated but not permitted, so retrying with the same credentials will keep failing.

faq.q: What should my API return for validation errors?
faq.a: 422 Unprocessable Content is the modern choice for well-formed requests with semantic errors. 400 works too but is vaguer about what went wrong.

faq.q: Is 418 a real status code?
faq.a: It started as an April Fools joke (RFC 2324) but is reserved and occasionally used playfully. You will not see it from serious APIs.

faq.q: What does 429 mean and how do I handle it?
faq.a: You hit a rate limit. Slow down, respect any Retry-After header, and use exponential backoff instead of hammering the endpoint.

ROT13 is Caesar with a fixed shift of 13, applied the same way both directions. Atbash mirrors the alphabet (A becomes Z, B becomes Y). Base64 is not a cipher but an encoding that turns any text, including Unicode, into plain ASCII safe for URLs and data fields.

These are classical ciphers for puzzles, learning and fun, not for protecting real secrets. Caesar, ROT13 and Atbash can be broken by hand in minutes. Never use them for passwords or private data; modern encryption like AES is what protects information for real.

faq.q: What is the Caesar cipher?
faq.a: A substitution cipher that shifts each letter by a fixed number of positions. With a shift of 3, A becomes D, B becomes E, and so on.

faq.q: What is ROT13 used for?
faq.a: Mostly for hiding spoilers and puzzle answers online. Applying ROT13 twice returns the original text, so the same operation encodes and decodes.

faq.q: How does Atbash work?
faq.a: It reverses the alphabet: A becomes Z, B becomes Y, C becomes X. Like ROT13, encoding and decoding are the same operation.

faq.q: Is Base64 encryption?
faq.a: No. Base64 is an encoding, not encryption: anyone can decode it instantly. It exists to represent binary or Unicode text in plain ASCII characters.

faq.q: Can I use these ciphers to protect passwords?
faq.a: No. Classical ciphers are trivially breakable and offer zero real security. Use a password manager and proper encryption instead.

explainer.body: Entropy measures password strength in bits: each bit doubles the number of guesses an attacker needs. A 40-bit password falls in seconds to modern hardware, while 80+ bits resist brute force for longer than the universe has existed. The score comes from password length multiplied by the size of the character pool it draws from.

Adding one character helps more than swapping letters for symbols. A 16-character passphrase of plain words can outscore an 8-character tangle of symbols, and it is far easier to remember. The crack-time estimate assumes 10 billion guesses per second, roughly a serious cracking rig.

faq.q: How many bits of entropy is enough?
faq.a: Aim for at least 80 bits for important accounts, which typically means 14+ random characters or a 5-6 word passphrase. Anything under 60 bits is crackable with modest resources.

faq.q: Does this work for passphrases too?
faq.a: The math assumes random characters, so multi-word passphrases score higher than their real strength if the words are common. For passphrases, count about 11-13 bits per random dictionary word instead.

faq.q: Is my password sent to a server?
faq.a: No. Analysis runs entirely in your browser. Never type a real password into any website you do not fully trust, including this one.

faq.q: Why is length more important than symbols?
faq.a: Each extra character multiplies the search space by the pool size. Going from 8 to 12 characters with the same character set multiplies guesses by the pool size four times over.

faq.q: What is the 10 billion guesses per second figure?
faq.a: A rough benchmark for a well-funded cracking setup against fast hashes. Slow, salted hashes used by good sites make real attacks far slower, but entropy is still the right way to compare passwords.

faq.q: When should I use ARIA?
faq.a: Only to fill gaps native HTML cannot cover, like custom sliders or tab widgets. Native elements come with keyboard behavior and semantics built in; ARIA only adds the semantics.

faq.q: What is the difference between aria-label and aria-labelledby?
faq.a: aria-label takes a literal string; aria-labelledby references visible elements by ID so the label stays in sync with what sighted users see. Prefer labelledby when visible text exists.

faq.q: Do ARIA attributes change how an element looks?
faq.a: No. They only affect what assistive technologies announce. All visual styling and keyboard behavior must still be implemented yourself.

faq.q: What are live regions?
faq.a: Elements with aria-live that announce dynamic updates to screen readers. Use polite for status messages and assertive only for urgent alerts.

faq.q: Can ARIA fix an inaccessible design?
faq.a: Rarely on its own. ARIA communicates meaning, but keyboard support, focus management and visible focus indicators must be built alongside it.

explainer.body: Basal Metabolic Rate is the energy your body needs for basic functions — breathing, circulation, cell repair — at complete rest. It is the baseline for any calorie plan: multiply it by an activity factor to get your total daily energy expenditure (TDEE).

Mifflin-St Jeor (1990) is the most widely validated for modern populations. The revised Harris-Benedict (1984) is the classic clinical standard. Both need gender, age, height and weight; results usually differ by less than 5%.

faq.q: Which formula should I use?
faq.a: Mifflin-St Jeor is generally preferred today and validated against more recent data. Harris-Benedict remains common in clinical settings. Try both and compare.

faq.q: Does BMR include exercise?
faq.a: No. BMR is rest only. For total daily calories, multiply your BMR by an activity factor (1.2 sedentary up to 1.9 very active).

faq.q: Why do men and women get different results?
faq.a: The formulas account for average differences in muscle mass and body composition between sexes at the same height and weight.

faq.q: How accurate is this?
faq.a: Within about 10% for most people. Muscle mass, hormones and medical conditions shift real BMR, so treat it as a starting estimate.

faq.q: Is my data stored?
faq.a: No. All calculation happens in your browser; nothing is sent or saved.

Ideal weight uses the Devine formula, the clinical standard. Ponderal index (weight over height cubed) is the corpulence index some researchers prefer over BMI.

Tape methods land within 3-4% of DEXA scans when measurements are careful — measure waist at the navel, relaxed, and keep the tape level. These are estimates for healthy adults, not medical diagnoses.

faq.q: Which method is most accurate?
faq.a: Navy body fat, when measured carefully, correlates well with DEXA. Lean mass and ideal weight are equations with wider error bands — useful as targets, not precise readings.

faq.q: How do I measure my waist correctly?
faq.a: At the navel (belly button), tape horizontal and snug but not compressing, after exhaling normally. Measure neck just below the Adam's apple, hip at the widest point.

faq.q: What is a healthy body fat percentage?
faq.a: Roughly 10-20% for men and 18-28% for women by most fitness standards; athletes run lower. Essential fat is about 3-5% for men and 10-13% for women.

faq.q: Ponderal index vs BMI?
faq.a: Ponderal index divides by height cubed instead of squared, which some researchers argue scales better across heights. Typical adult values fall between 11 and 15 kg/m³.

faq.q: Is this medical advice?
faq.a: No. These are general estimates. Consult a professional for health decisions, especially if you have a medical condition.

faq.q: How fast will I lose weight on a 500 kcal deficit?
faq.a: Roughly 0.5 kg (about 1 lb) per week on average, since a kilogram of body fat stores around 7,700 kcal. Real loss varies with water weight and adherence.

faq.q: Should I eat back exercise calories?
faq.a: No — your activity level already accounts for exercise. Eating back estimates from fitness trackers usually overcounts and stalls progress.

faq.q: Is a bigger deficit faster?
faq.a: Up to a point, but very large deficits cost muscle, energy and adherence. A 500-750 kcal deficit is the sustainable sweet spot for most people.

faq.q: Do I need to hit the target exactly every day?
faq.a: No. Weekly average matters more than any single day. Aim to land within about 10% of target across the week.

faq.q: Is this medical advice?
faq.a: No. This is a general estimate for healthy adults. Talk to a doctor or dietitian if you have a medical condition, are pregnant, or are under 18.

explainer.body: Your input is parsed into a neutral in-memory structure, then serialized to the target format. JSON, XML, CSV, TSV, INI and TOML are handled by built-in parsers that work fully offline; YAML uses the js-yaml library loaded from a CDN. XML attributes map to @-prefixed keys, CSV and TSV become arrays of row objects, and INI sections become nested objects.

Conversions are structural, not magic: deeply nested data flattens awkwardly into CSV rows, and INI only supports one level of sections. TOML support covers the common subset (key/value pairs, sections, arrays, basic types). For YAML you need a network connection the first time the library loads.

faq.q: Is my data uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Parsing and serialization run entirely in your browser. Only the optional YAML library is fetched from a CDN; your data never leaves the page.

faq.q: Why does my CSV conversion look flat?
faq.a: CSV is a tabular format, so nested objects are represented as row objects with one column per key. Deeply nested structures convert best to JSON, XML, YAML or TOML instead.

faq.q: How are XML attributes handled?
faq.a: Attributes become keys prefixed with @ (for example @id), and mixed text content lands in a #text key, so a round-trip back to XML preserves them.

faq.q: Does it validate my input?
faq.a: Yes. Malformed JSON or XML produces a clear error message instead of a partial result, so you know exactly what to fix.

faq.q: Can I convert without a network connection?
faq.a: For JSON, XML, CSV, TSV, INI and TOML, yes — everything is built in. YAML is the only format that needs the CDN library.

faq.q: Why is AVIF missing or disabled?

faq.q: Can I convert HEIC photos from my iPhone?

faq.q: Does converting reduce quality?
faq.a: Lossy formats (JPG, WebP, AVIF) lose a little detail depending on the quality slider. PNG and BMP are lossless. Converting from a lossy source to another lossy format compounds the loss slightly.

faq.q: Is there a file size limit?

faq.q: Is my JSON sent to a server?

faq.q: How are nested objects handled?

faq.q: What happens with null values?

faq.q: Can I change the root type name?

faq.q: Does it handle arrays of mixed types?
faq.a: Arrays are typed from the first non-null item. Heterogeneous arrays fall back to the language's generic type (any, Any, object, dynamic).

explainer.body: X% of Y answers everyday percent problems like tips, discounts and tax (20% of 150 = 30). Percentage difference compares two values symmetrically — order does not matter. Percentage error measures how far a measurement is from the true value, the standard in science and engineering.

Percentage difference divides by the average of the two values, so it is symmetric. Percent change (or increase/decrease) divides by the starting value instead, so direction matters. This toolkit uses the symmetric difference formula.

faq.q: What is the formula for X% of Y?
faq.a: Multiply Y by X divided by 100. For example, 20% of 150 = 150 × 0.20 = 30.

faq.q: How is percentage difference calculated?
faq.a: Absolute difference divided by the average of the two values, times 100: |V1−V2| / ((V1+V2)/2) × 100.

faq.q: What is percentage error used for?
faq.a: It quantifies measurement accuracy: |measured − true| / |true| × 100. Lower is better; 0% means a perfect measurement.

faq.q: Can I use decimals and negatives?
faq.a: Yes. All three calculators accept decimals, negatives and very large numbers.

faq.q: Is anything I type stored?

explainer.body: The Riegel formula (T2 = T1 × (D2/D1)^1.06) scales a known performance to other distances. It is well validated for trained runners across 5K to marathon. Enter your best recent time at any of the four distances and all four predictions update, each with its required average pace.
The marathon splits table shows even pacing every 5 km — the strategy behind most personal bests. Aim to hit each split within a few seconds; banking time early usually backfires after 30 km.

faq.q: How accurate is the Riegel formula?
faq.a: Within a few percent for trained runners on similar courses. It assumes equivalent fitness and conditions — heat, hills and wind all shift real times.

faq.q: Can I predict from a non-race time trial?
faq.a: Yes, if it was a true maximal effort. Predictions from easy runs will be far too optimistic.

faq.q: Why 1.06 as the exponent?
faq.a: It is Riegel's empirically fitted value from world-record data. Some coaches use 1.05-1.08 for specific populations, but 1.06 is the standard.

faq.q: Does it work for ultramarathons?
faq.a: Not reliably. The formula breaks down past the marathon as fatigue, fueling and terrain dominate.

faq.q: Is my data stored?
faq.a: No. Everything is computed locally in your browser.
